properties.name: The first real usage report on reflow2's own graph: 113 calls over 31 tools in 3¼ hours, and 4 of 5 refusals landed in `other` — an argument-shape refusal has no class yet
properties.statement: Read 2026-09-12 18:07Z with `usage_report(peek)` on the window since the ledger began (14:52Z, when #490's binary went live): 113 calls, 31 distinct tools, 150 of 181 never called; loop_status ×26 (the Stop hook's nudge plus deliberate checks), record_finding ×13, pin_at_epoch ×10 (the release cut), export_graph ×8. Refusals: 5 — one `refused` (export_graph on a stale binary, correct) and FOUR `other`: three record_finding and one add_design_rule, all the same phrasing — rmcp's deserialiser saying "invalid type: string … expected a sequence", when the harness serialised a new list parameter (`steps`) as a string because its cached tool schema predated it. So the very first report did what the skill says a large `other` does: it named a refusal class the table lacks. An `invalid_argument` class (a parameter present but of the wrong shape) is owed, beside missing_argument and unknown_argument. Two more limits seen: 22 of 113 calls carry the client name `rmcp 3.3.0` — a proxy that re-initialises after a daemon respawn declares rmcp's default client info, not the harness's — and 37 seats were minted in one afternoon, one per respawn or probe, so `seats` counts connections rather than people. Anthony's prompt for the read: an unofficial observation that tool calls per step had gone up (they had — independent calls are batched, up to ~20 in one step); the ledger has no baseline before today, so the per-session rate is the next report's comparison, not this one's.
